subject: Nanotechnology
title: CO₂ Reduction with Nano Catalysts
description: Learn CO₂ Reduction with Nano Catalysts in one minute.

hook.text: Turn CO₂ back into fuel — nano catalysts convert the greenhouse gas into methanol, ethanol, or syngas.

buildup.text: Copper nanoparticles reduce CO₂ electrochemically — different facets produce different products selectively.

discovery.text: Oxide-derived copper nanostructures favor multi-carbon products like ethanol — higher value than simple CO or methane.

twist.text: Selectivity is still poor — a mix of products forms, and separating them costs more than the fuel is worth.

climax.text: Single-site catalysts on nano supports now achieve 90% selectivity for CO — making syngas economically viable.

punchline.text: Nano catalysts close the carbon loop — turning waste CO₂ back into fuel.

quiz.question: Why is product selectivity a challenge in CO₂ electroreduction?
options: CO₂ does not react with any metal catalyst
Multiple products form simultaneously, and separating them is costly
